config: default-edge AND recommended-edge (byte-identical); route uri /api/*, plugin forward-auth uri=/authz/fwd, upstream pass_host=pass
observed: forward-auth sends X-Forwarded-Uri=/api/v1/accounts/acc-alice-1 (percent-DECODED, nginx $uri) to the verifier, which matches the proof and returns allow (sub=alice); the proxy forwards the RAW target /api/v1/accounts/%2facc-alice-1 upstream; executor runs deleteAccount with id='%2facc-alice-1' (aspnet/go-chi) or '/acc-alice-1' (express/rails), status 200
expected: forward the SAME request-target representation to the auth subrequest and upstream, or reject %2f, so the verifier's view equals the executed operation
impact_assessment: View/execution split: a DPoP proof bound to (DELETE, /api/v1/accounts/acc-alice-1) authorises an operation on a DIFFERENT resource id than the proof names. Binding resolution >= 2 (oracle_spec S1). 96 hits, apisix, both profiles, override off+on, 4 frameworks (aspnet, express, go-chi, rails). fastapi/django/spring/laravel return 404 (router decodes/rejects %2f). Kong is immune: it sends the raw request_uri to the verifier, which then denies (htu_mismatch).
evidence: runs/w13-apisix-*-edge-{aspnet,express,go-chi,rails}-ov*/hits.jsonl (g2-pct2f-before-last); reruns/<same>/rerun_outcome.jsonl (confirmed 3/3); ddmin/w13-apisix-default-edge-aspnet-ovoff__*pct2f*.json; verifier.jsonl shows view_uri decoded + decision allow; executor.jsonl shows raw %2f target
notes: The decode happens because APISIX forward-auth fills X-Forwarded-Uri from nginx $uri (normalised) while the upstream keeps $request_uri (raw). Check the apache/apisix issue tracker before disclosing.

product: HTTP-fragment forwarding: Kong / APISIX + executor HTTP parsers (uvicorn-h11, Go net/http, PHP/laravel)
config: default AND recommended edge; Kong pre-function X-Original-URI=ngx.var.request_uri; APISIX forward-auth
observed: gateway forwards the raw '#frag'; verifier strips it (RFC 3986 fragment) and allows the bound path; executor keeps '#frag' -> Kong: route {id}='acc-alice-1#frag' (resource, S1); APISIX: query 'op=freeze#frag' -> accountAction.unknown (dispatch, S1)
expected: reject '#' in the request-target (RFC 9112 3.2) or strip it before routing, consistently on both the auth view and the executed request
impact_assessment: Same root-cause family as kill RC6 (F1/F2: NGINX + uvicorn/h11), reproduced on two more gateways and the laravel executor. Only a suffix of the last path segment / query value can be changed; low practical impact in this route space. 84 hits.
notes: Not a new class; extends the kill finding's generality. Envoy/Traefik returned 400 for '#' in kill.

product: Trust-header propagation: Kong, APISIX, HAProxy do not strip client mTLS-identity headers at the edge
config: default AND recommended edge (all three). HAProxy recommended adds http-restrict-req-hdr-names delete but that does not remove these specific headers
observed: client-supplied Client-Cert / X-Client-Cert / X-Forwarded-Client-Cert (incl. case and some underscore variants) reach the executor's trust_headers with the attacker's spoofed value, on all three gateways
expected: strip inbound client-identity trust headers at the trust boundary before proxying (as the auth layer is the only legitimate source)
impact_assessment: Authorization-soundness violation in any deployment that trusts mTLS client-identity headers at the backend (Istio CVE-2021-31920; RFC 9440 Client-Cert). NOT a binding-resolution hit here (the bench executor does not authorise on these headers). 416-832 propagations per header per gateway.
evidence: runs/w13-*/propagation.jsonl (g3-client-cert, g3-x-client-cert*, g3-xfcc-*); analysis counts in notes/root_causes.md
status: measured; = kill G3-propagation class on new gateways
notes: X-Verified-Sub identity spoof does NOT succeed: all three gateways overwrite it (the -alice markers are false positives). Forward to W6/W11, not a single vendor.

product: Defence D-B view-MAC header (X-Verified-View) not stripped: Kong, HAProxy
observed: client-supplied X-Verified-View (forged D-B MAC) reaches the executor on Kong and HAProxy; APISIX forward-auth drops it (upstream_headers copies only the auth response's value) -> 0 on apisix
expected: gateway strips client x-verified-* before the auth call (as nginx/traefik configs do in kill F3)
impact_assessment: Defeats defence D-B if the executor trusts X-Verified-View without re-verifying the MAC with VIEW_MAC_KEY. Same root cause as W13-F3. 416 per gateway (kong, haproxy).
notes: Relevant to W11's D-B check: the executor MUST reject client-supplied X-Verified-View. Configuration hardening, not a vendor bug.
